question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
analysis: The patient's symptoms include weakness in extending the middle finger and radial deviation upon wrist extension, without sensory loss. These symptoms suggest an issue with a nerve that primarily controls motor function to the extensor muscles of the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, fits this description as it innervates the extensor muscles of the forearm and does not carry significant sensory fibers. The ulnar nerve primarily affects the medial hand and fingers, the anterior interosseous nerve affects flexor muscles, the superficial radial nerve is primarily sensory, and the musculocutaneous nerve affects the anterior compartment of the arm. Therefore, the posterior interosseous nerve is the most likely affected nerve in this scenario.
